clue.text: Drawing a boat, make notes about it

indicators.note: the singing goes round the boat, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to make notes with the voice is to sing
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An artist sketching a boat jots down notes around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make notes' looks like jotting things down, but here it means using the voice. 'about' wraps the singing round the boat; 'it' just points back to the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a rough picture with pencil is the act described by the noun drawing.

clue.text: A tradesman who puts people in their place?

definitions.text: A tradesman who puts people in their place?

parts.words: A tradesman who puts people in their place?
parts.note: read literally, a person who stations others, positioning them where they belong; really a shopkeeper selling paper and pens

explanation.definitionFit: A seller of writing paper, envelopes and pens is a tradesman; the word looks like one who stations people.

clue.text: Relation's uplifting note brings cheer

indicators.note: lifting up letters out of the word Relation's, taking a run from inside it

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A relative's cheerful musical note lifts everyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' seems to praise the note; here it lifts ELAT out of 'Relation's', and the note E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to make them joyful, the verb sense of making happy.

clue.text: A minister's tea — quite simple

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
plain means simple, unadorned

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes his tea without frills.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a chapel, regiment or hospital is a kind of minister of religion.

clue.text: Scheme to raise interest

explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret scheme, and to fascinate someone is to raise their interest.

clue.text: A stone fish-trap

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a net is a trap for catching fish

explanation.surface: A stone used as a fish-trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red semi-precious gem is a kind of precious stone.

clue.text: A big "thank you" is called for here in Italy

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for very big
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Italy a great vote of thanks is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for outsize; 'is called for' only joins. AOSTA is a town in north-west Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Alpine north-west of the country, so a place one could be in Italy.

clue.text: He may be warned if crooked

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so the letters of warned are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man might be cautioned if he is dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' suggests a criminal being warned; it signals rearranging WARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so a male person the pronoun could stand for.

clue.text: Watches a fly going up and down

parts.note: to watch is to see
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Someone observes an insect bobbing up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as the insect, but it is a verb: to WING is to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving alternately upward and downward like a playground plank on a pivot.

clue.text: Equally determined to secure an item of value

parts.note: as, as in as good as, means equally
set on something means determined

explanation.surface: A resolute effort to obtain something worth having.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful or valuable possession, a sense used in accounting and everyday speech.

clue.text: A senseless setback a body of conservationists find hard

indicators.note: set back means turned backwards, so the word for senseless is read in reverse

parts.note: mad means senseless
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation body

explanation.surface: Conservationists stubbornly resist a foolish reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns the word for senseless backwards. The body of conservationists is the National Trust, which looks after historic British buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding, as the old word for an impossibly hard stone suggests.

clue.text: Soldiers with gear to pay for

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
dress means clothing or gear

explanation.surface: Troops with kit that must be paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends or compensate for a wrong is to pay for it.

clue.text: Thought by many to be perfect

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for many

explanation.surface: Something many people regard as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece by the other; 'many' as L (fifty) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Representing flawless excellence, a synonym for perfect.

clue.text: Coarse yet popular English member, a worker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a leg is a limb or member
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A crude but well-liked English member of a workers' group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or refinement, a near synonym of unrefined and crude.

clue.text: Usual tin put out for shellfish

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting out a can for seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cephalopod mollusc with a spiral chambered shell, loosely a shellfish.

clue.text: A bilingual graduate dropped but not disconcerted

parts.note: una means a in both Spanish and Italian, so it is a word for a in two languages
BA is a Bachelor of Arts
shed means dropped or cast off

explanation.surface: A graduate fluent in two languages was dismissed but remained unruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bilingual' reads as a description of the graduate; it is A in two languages at once, Spanish and Italian UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Unembarrassed and composed, the opposite of flustered.

clue.text: Raise an objection when there's reason

definitions.meaning: to object, as in do you ...?

explanation.definitionFit: To object is to care or take exception, and the intellect is the seat of reasoning.

clue.text: Small daughter is offensive, but let off

parts.note: D is the short form of daughter
a charge is an attack or offensive

explanation.surface: A little girl is rude but gets off unpunished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like rudeness; it is a noun, a military CHARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing a weapon or releasing someone from duty are both senses of letting off.

clue.text: The subject matter affords satisfaction

definitions.meaning: what a book or document contains

explanation.definitionFit: What a book holds is its material, and something that pleases makes a person happy.

clue.text: Criminal beast repeatedly put inside

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for the beast appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden
in, as of a prisoner held inside

explanation.surface: A felon is jailed again and again like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer is a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Writing about a right back

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A report on a footballer playing at right back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' suggests a football position. 'Writing' only sets the scene of a match report.
explanation.definitionFit: The hind part of something is its back.

clue.text: Hands over evidence after study

indicators.note: after places the evidence after the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
signs are evidence or indications

explanation.surface: A detective delivers proof after looking into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign is to deliver or entrust goods into someone's keeping.

clue.text: Put bet on after half-time only

indicators.note: after places the word for bet on after the half
half here takes the back half of the word time, its final two letters

parts.note: to rely on is to bet on, to count on

explanation.surface: Place a wager after the interval in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the interval in a match; 'half' takes the second half of 'time'. 'Put' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Just, no more than, a synonym of only.

clue.text: Try once more!

parts.note: not a plea to keep going but a court trying a case a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Courts try cases, so to listen to a case again is to try it a second time.

clue.text: New Testament's declaration

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A formal announcement in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' looks like a single phrase; 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal announcement or assertion is a declaration.

clue.text: Checks supporters

definitions.meaning: halts or delays, as a stay of execution
ropes holding up a mast, or corset bones

explanation.definitionFit: A postponement halts proceedings, and ropes bracing a mast hold it up.

clue.text: A quarter remains almost submerged

parts.note: W is west, one of the four compass quarters
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Part of the ruins lies nearly underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Level with the surface of the water so that waves wash over it, nearly sunk.

clue.text: Lounge bagged by an outsider

indicators.note: bagged by means held inside, so the lounge word goes within an

parts.note: to lie is to lounge about

explanation.surface: A sofa is captured by a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room; it is a verb, to LIE about.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner or stranger is an outsider.

clue.text: The runner from Blackheath let everybody pass him

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A runner from a London district lets the whole field overtake him.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackheath is a district of south-east London. 'pass him' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in track events is a runner.

clue.text: Meaner, so retains change

indicators.note: change says the letters of retains are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A stingier person keeps the coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests coins kept; it signals rearranging RETAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: More spiteful or unkind, a comparative synonym of meaner.

clue.text: Mention about five hundred pounds with some regret

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for mention goes round the other letters

parts.note: to say is to mention
D is the Roman numeral for 500
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Remarking ruefully on a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretfully, an adverb of sorrow.

clue.text: One trains to break a horse, that's well-known

indicators.note: to break means to shatter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainer sets out to break in a famous horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' suggests breaking in a horse; it signals rearranging ONE TRAINS. ROSINANTE is Don Quixote's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous nag ridden by Don Quixote in Cervantes's novel.
